note: Immediate rows (pdf 57): the operand is the word after the instruction (Fig 3.2.5, pdf 49). Every expect value is read from the cited page image and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation. Bus offsets follow the data access figures (pdf 29 read, pdf 31 write) with the effective address PC+1. C46 (CMP direction) is stated in each CMPI derivation.

vectors.cite: Immediate table, MVII row, pdf 57; Fig 3.2.5, pdf 49; data access timing figure, pdf 29
vectors.derivation: The immediate table (pdf 57) prints MVII I, DDD as 1010 111 DDD followed by the word iiiiii IIII III III, 8 cycles, 'MoVe In Immediate data to register DDD from PC+1', no status change. DDD = 001 (R1): R1 = $1234, the word at $1001. Fig 3.2.5 (pdf 49): EA <- PC+1, PC <- PC+2, so R7 goes $1000 -> $1002. C51: the operand word keeps all 16 bits on the flat test bus. Flags keep their initial values (all 0). Bus (pdf 29, instruction fetch and data access, indirect register mode; immediate mode is that access with the effective address PC+1 per Fig 3.2.5, pdf 49): FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000, then the BAR that puts out the effective address at cycle 4, a READ of $1001 (data in at cycle 6); the unit is the printed 8 cycles. The row has no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible goes 0 -> 1. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.
